title: DeSantis mocks Anthropic CEO for inviting religious leaders to bless his AI model
source_used: Florida Politics (first reporter of the remarks); Economic Times video page had no text
key_facts: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis spoke on Tuesday, 6 Oct 2026, in West Palm Beach.
He criticised Anthropic for having religious leaders in San Francisco bless the idea that its AI chatbot is sentient.
He said an AI chatbot 'doesn't have a soul' and called the discussion 'a really creepy thing'.
He asked who would make victims whole if AI agents hacked financial institutions and liquidated accounts, and said companies may not have the money to pay.
He said an AI bill of rights would protect name, image and likeness, intellectual property and privacy; he has so far failed to get it passed.
The article notes that Pope Leo XIV's encyclical Magnifica Humanitas earlier this year made similar points.
quote_evidence: An AI chatbot doesn’t have a soul.
DeSantis has tried, and thus far failed, to get a so-called AI bill of rights passed.
why_it_matters_hint: A governor's push for AI rights and liability protections bears on state and federal AI rules.
notes: Economic Times (7 Oct) video page had no text on fetch, so ET is not the source. Florida Politics (A.G. Gancarski) is the first reporter. Event before 7 Oct: stale, score lowered 6 to 5 (-1).
